finding.summary: Unbounded range expansion amplifies attacker-controlled data extent into unbounded reference enumeration (resource-exhaustion DoS across all collaborators)
finding.evidence: `resolveRange` fills an omitted endpoint from `bounds` max (`{ r: b.r ?? max.r, c: b.c ?? max.c }`), and `bounds` comes from `CellIndex.bounds()` — the min/max of *any* populated cell, with no density check and no clamp. Every consumer then materializes the range cell-by-cell: `MemStore.buildDependantsMap` and `YorkieStore.buildDependantsMap` do `toSrefs(extractReferences(expandUnboundedRanges(cell.f, bounds)))`, `calculator.ts` does `sheet.fetchGridByReferences(references)`, and `Arguments.iterate` walks `toSrefs([node.v])` calling `grid.get(ref)` per cell. Attack: a collaborator writes one cell far out (e.g. `A1048576`) plus one formula `=SUM(A:A)`; on every subsequent edit each client rebuilds the dependants map, expanding a 4-character reference into ~1e6 Set entries per formula (and `A:B` into maxR×maxC), hanging/OOMing every connected client. Before this change the cost of a range was bounded by the literal text the author typed; now it is derived from other cells' positions, which in YorkieStore come from the untrusted shared CRDT document (`this.cellIndex.bounds()` at yorkie-store.ts, `getUsedBounds`/`buildDependantsMap`) and are never validated. No cap or guard against the expanded cell count appears anywhere in the diff.
